subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Roasting Software and Data Logging
description: A fast breakdown of Roasting Software and Data Logging for builders.

hook.text: Modern roasters use software like Cropster and Artisan to log every second of a roast as a replicable digital profile.

buildup.text: Temperature probes in the bean mass and exhaust track real-time data. Rate of rise, development time, and airflow are plotted.

discovery.text: Once a great roast is achieved, the profile is saved. Future batches follow the same curve, ensuring consistency.

twist.text: Day-to-day variables—ambient temperature, humidity, batch size—still require real-time adjustments despite the data.

climax.text: The best roasters use data as a guide, not a dogma. Intuition and senses fill the gaps that numbers can't capture.

punchline.text: Data tells you what happened. Senses tell you what to do next.

quiz.question: Why can't roasters just follow the same digital profile every time?
options: Day-to-day variables like temperature and humidity require real-time adjustments

details.summary: Modern roasting software captures bean temperature, rate of rise, airflow, and gas settings in real time. Roasters overlay past profiles to replicate successful batches or diagnose problems. Data logging transformed roasting from intuitive craft to repeatable science.
details.whyItMatters: Software and data logging let roasters scale quality consistently. Without them, every batch would rely entirely on the roaster's memory and senses.
takeaways: Software tracks temperature, rate of rise, and input settings live
Overlaying reference profiles ensures batch-to-batch consistency
Popular platforms include Cropster and Artisan

faq.question: What data points does roasting software typically track?
faq.answer: Core data includes bean temperature, environmental temperature, rate of rise, gas or power settings, airflow position, and drum speed. Advanced systems also log humidity, weight loss, and color measurements.

faq.question: Can roasting software control the roaster automatically?
faq.answer: Some modern systems offer profile playback that adjusts gas and airflow to match a saved reference curve. However, most specialty roasters prefer manual control with software guidance, intervening when conditions require it.
